import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import io

# Dataset string provided by the user
data = """survived,pclass,sex,age,sibsp,parch,fare,embarked,class,who,adult_male,deck,embark_town,alive,alone
0,3,male,22.0,1,0,7.25,S,Third,man,True,,Southampton,no,False
1,1,female,38.0,1,0,71.2833,C,First,woman,False,C,Cherbourg,yes,False
1,3,female,26.0,0,0,7.925,S,Third,woman,False,,Southampton,yes,True
1,1,female,35.0,1,0,53.1,S,First,woman,False,C,Southampton,yes,False
0,3,male,35.0,0,0,8.05,S,Third,man,True,,Southampton,no,True
"""

# Load the dataset into a pandas DataFrame
df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(data))

# Map 'survived' numerical values to descriptive labels for better readability in plots
df['survived_label'] = df['survived'].map({0: 'Did Not Survive', 1: 'Survived'})

# Set a visually appealing style for seaborn plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", palette="viridis")

# Create a figure and a set of subplots (2 rows, 2 columns)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(16, 12))
fig.suptitle('Titanic Survival Analysis by Key Features', fontsize=18, y=1.02) # Overall title

# Plot 1: Survival Rate by Passenger Class and Sex
sns.barplot(data=df, x='pclass', y='survived', hue='sex', ax=axes[0, 0])
axes[0, 0].set_title('Survival Rate by Passenger Class and Sex', fontsize=14)
axes[0, 0].set_ylabel('Survival Rate', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 0].set_xlabel('Passenger Class', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 0].tick_params(axis='both', which='major', labelsize=10)
axes[0, 0].legend(title='Sex', fontsize=10, title_fontsize=12)

# Plot 2: Age Distribution by Survival Status
# Drop NaN values in 'age' for KDE plot if present in a larger dataset
sns.kdeplot(data=df.dropna(subset=['age']), x='age', hue='survived_label', fill=True, common_norm=False, ax=axes[0, 1])
axes[0, 1].set_title('Age Distribution by Survival Status', fontsize=14)
axes[0, 1].set_xlabel('Age', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 1].set_ylabel('Density', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 1].tick_params(axis='both', which='major', labelsize=10)
axes[0, 1].legend(title='Survival Status', fontsize=10, title_fontsize=12)

# Plot 3: Fare Distribution by Survival Status
# Drop NaN values in 'fare' for KDE plot
sns.kdeplot(data=df.dropna(subset=['fare']), x='fare', hue='survived_label', fill=True, common_norm=False, ax=axes[1, 0])
axes[1, 0].set_title('Fare Distribution by Survival Status', fontsize=14)
axes[1, 0].set_xlabel('Fare', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 0].set_ylabel('Density', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 0].tick_params(axis='both', which='major', labelsize=10)
axes[1, 0].legend(title='Survival Status', fontsize=10, title_fontsize=12)

# Plot 4: Age vs Fare by Survival Status and Sex
# Drop NaN values in 'age' or 'fare' for scatter plot
sns.scatterplot(data=df.dropna(subset=['age', 'fare']), x='age', y='fare', hue='survived_label', style='sex', alpha=0.7, ax=axes[1, 1])
axes[1, 1].set_title('Age vs Fare by Survival Status and Sex', fontsize=14)
axes[1, 1].set_xlabel('Age', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 1].set_ylabel('Fare', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 1].tick_params(axis='both', which='major', labelsize=10)
# Place legend outside the plot area to prevent overlap with data points
axes[1, 1].legend(title_fontsize=12, fontsize=10, loc='upper left', bbox_to_anchor=(1, 1))

# Adjust layout to prevent labels/titles/legends from overlapping
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.95, 1]) # Adjust rect to make space for the legend on the right

# Save the plot to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')

# Close the plot to free memory
plt.close()
